newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen higher at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open higher on Monday, taking last week's record-high run even further.
Analysts said the absence of economic data today cleared the way for the market to climb though they said the momentum was likely to slow later in the week.
"The market continues to do well. Obviously there is a lot of enthusiasm for stocks and I think this will continue," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Key economic data due this week include the consumer price index and industrial production figures. Also, Friday is the so-called triple-witching expiration of futures and options.
"I am looking for another good day and a reasonable opening," said Thome Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood.
"But I think the momentum is going to dissipate by the end of the week," Brown said.
On Friday, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 70.57 points to a record close of 7782, its sixth consecutive record.
For the week, the Dow gained about 346 points while the Nasdaq composite rose 18 points to 1,423.
The benchmark 30-year long bond was up 5/32 with a 6.71 percent yield. The Standard & Poor's futures index was up 1.05 to 904.45.
Japan's Nikkei average closed higher, up 152.72 points, or 0.74 percent, at 20,681.07. In London, the FTSE 100 was down 38.2 points at 4744.9. U.S. stocks were quiet in London.
The dollar was easier against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 113.98/08 yen. In Europe, the dollar was trading at 1.7318/30 marks.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that large lenders are paying a premium for consumer loans while saving money in efficient processing and collection in the belief they can profit from Americans' tendency to live beyoned their means.
